spec.title: Keep form sign-in from stalling before Settings opens
spec.scope:
Repair the reported intermittent session-activation timeout in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts, case 'signed-out Settings entry returns to protected Settings after form sign-in'. Preserve the real email/password/challenge form journey and distinguish active Clerk session, automatic Settings destination, and local API authorization.

## Evidence and diagnosis boundary
The owner's reported 68/70 run is separate from the available playwright-report/index.html report (69 total, 69 expected, no unexpected/flaky/skipped cases; both sign-in cases passed). The available report and last-run markers do not recover the reported failure's project, exact error or stack. Do not invent that signature or call the older pass a reproduction. Recover existing redacted evidence, or reproduce through the admitted browser-tests diagnostic before attributing a root cause. Record project, case, failed stage, timing, and exact redacted assertion signature. The reported activation failure is owned repair scope, not an ignored baseline.

The current submitSignInForm fills email and password, waits at most 12 seconds for an optional verification textbox, and submits 424242 only when it becomes visible in that window. The caller then waits separately up to 30 seconds for Clerk.loaded and Clerk.session.id, then for /settings and HTTP 200 from /api/auth/user. A late challenge can therefore appear after challenge observation ended, and accepting a code can remove its controls automatically. These are candidate race boundaries, not proven causes. A failure before an active session is not evidence that fallbackRedirectUrl or local approval is broken. client/src/App.tsx already passes the allow-listed return path to SignIn.fallbackRedirectUrl.

## Repair steps
1. Run the sealed revision's Agent-first preflight with its generated TASK_ID and TASK_PLAN_FILE and test-heavy before any implementation or workload. Confirm actual owner authorization covers this unchanged split repair; preparation and guard validity alone do not authorize execution. Restore the sealed plan through gate:restore-plan in a fresh environment when needed.
2. Recover or reproduce the exact failure at the challenge/session boundary using the supported bound browser-tests diagnostic. Preserve first-failure evidence; a passing retry proves only intermittency. Do not retry the whole suite to hide a failure or use programmatic sign-in as proof of form navigation.
3. Apply the smallest evidence-supported repair. Prefer a test-local, deadline-bound challenge/session coordinator if the form helper stops observing the challenge too early: observe session activation and a supported challenge together, allow a challenge that arrives after the old 12-second window but within the activation budget, submit each challenge at most once, tolerate controls disappearing after automatic submission, and finish only on an active session. Use one finite total activation deadline (retain the current 30-second activation budget rather than stacking new waits), bounded polling/action waits and no recovery after context closure. Surface persistent errors rather than silently swallowing them. Do not add blind page reloads, repeat password submissions, provider changes or a generic outage-retry framework. If evidence instead implicates production session lifecycle, amend the concrete affected scope and boundary assertions through the supported route before editing production behavior; do not change routing merely because a session never activated.
4. Keep browser.newContext with empty cookies/origins, official testing-token routing installed before navigation, and finally context.close. Keep the real-form case independent of tests/fixtures.ts's saved owner session and ticket-sign-in recovery. Do not mutate shared storage state or substitute activateTestSession/clerkTesting.signIn for this case. Leave the separate unsafe-target test's programmatic helper and explicit navigation semantics intact.
5. If challenge/recovery helpers change, add deterministic controlled-clock/event-order browser tests in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts at that helper boundary: a challenge arriving after the old observation window but within budget eventually activates; no-challenge immediate success works; disappearing controls after code acceptance do not trigger another submission; a challenge that never completes or a persistent terminal error fails within the single deadline without duplicate submissions. These tests may simulate the helper's observations but must not replace the separate real-provider form journey. Check this file is actually selected by browser-tests.
6. Deliver bounded, allow-listed failure diagnostics (stage, elapsed milliseconds, pathname without query/fragment, booleans for Clerk loaded/session present/challenge visible, bounded known error codes and HTTP status only). Limit collection to 2 seconds and serialized output to 2 KiB; diagnostic collection failure must not mask the original assertion. Never log credentials, verification input, session/user IDs, cookies, storage state, tokens, request/response bodies, arbitrary DOM text, full URLs, raw provider errors or traces containing submitted credentials. If diagnostics code changes, include deterministic assertions that sensitive sentinel inputs and URL queries/fragments never appear and truncation/collection timeout preserves the original failure.
7. Run the complete bound test-heavy workload once the coherent repair is ready. A supported filtered browser-tests run is diagnosis only and cannot establish full-tier PASS. Preserve the empty baseline catalog; classify unrelated failures honestly rather than expanding this repair or inventing exclusions. Record all not-reached/failed steps and applicable target/revision evidence.

Photo filename/image/reload assertions (separate split repair), broad Clerk provisioning-outage recovery already described by task 820, provider configuration, SDK upgrades without evidence, gate maintenance, new baseline entries, production deployment and independent verification tasks. Increasing waits alone, enabling whole-suite retries, relaxing authentication/approval, or replacing the form with a testing ticket does not satisfy this repair.

# Keep form sign-in from stalling before Settings opens

## Scope
Repair the reported intermittent session-activation timeout in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts, case 'signed-out Settings entry returns to protected Settings after form sign-in'. Preserve the real email/password/challenge form journey and distinguish active Clerk session, automatic Settings destination, and local API authorization.

## Evidence and diagnosis boundary
The owner's reported 68/70 run is separate from the available playwright-report/index.html report (69 total, 69 expected, no unexpected/flaky/skipped cases; both sign-in cases passed). The available report and last-run markers do not recover the reported failure's project, exact error or stack. Do not invent that signature or call the older pass a reproduction. Recover existing redacted evidence, or reproduce through the admitted browser-tests diagnostic before attributing a root cause. Record project, case, failed stage, timing, and exact redacted assertion signature. The reported activation failure is owned repair scope, not an ignored baseline.

The current submitSignInForm fills email and password, waits at most 12 seconds for an optional verification textbox, and submits 424242 only when it becomes visible in that window. The caller then waits separately up to 30 seconds for Clerk.loaded and Clerk.session.id, then for /settings and HTTP 200 from /api/auth/user. A late challenge can therefore appear after challenge observation ended, and accepting a code can remove its controls automatically. These are candidate race boundaries, not proven causes. A failure before an active session is not evidence that fallbackRedirectUrl or local approval is broken. client/src/App.tsx already passes the allow-listed return path to SignIn.fallbackRedirectUrl.

## Repair steps
1. Run the sealed revision's Agent-first preflight with its generated TASK_ID and TASK_PLAN_FILE and test-heavy before any implementation or workload. Confirm actual owner authorization covers this unchanged split repair; preparation and guard validity alone do not authorize execution. Restore the sealed plan through gate:restore-plan in a fresh environment when needed.
2. Recover or reproduce the exact failure at the challenge/session boundary using the supported bound browser-tests diagnostic. Preserve first-failure evidence; a passing retry proves only intermittency. Do not retry the whole suite to hide a failure or use programmatic sign-in as proof of form navigation.
3. Apply the smallest evidence-supported repair. Prefer a test-local, deadline-bound challenge/session coordinator if the form helper stops observing the challenge too early: observe session activation and a supported challenge together, allow a challenge that arrives after the old 12-second window but within the activation budget, submit each challenge at most once, tolerate controls disappearing after automatic submission, and finish only on an active session. Use one finite total activation deadline (retain the current 30-second activation budget rather than stacking new waits), bounded polling/action waits and no recovery after context closure. Surface persistent errors rather than silently swallowing them. Do not add blind page reloads, repeat password submissions, provider changes or a generic outage-retry framework. If evidence instead implicates production session lifecycle, amend the concrete affected scope and boundary assertions through the supported route before editing production behavior; do not change routing merely because a session never activated.
4. Keep browser.newContext with empty cookies/origins, official testing-token routing installed before navigation, and finally context.close. Keep the real-form case independent of tests/fixtures.ts's saved owner session and ticket-sign-in recovery. Do not mutate shared storage state or substitute activateTestSession/clerkTesting.signIn for this case. Leave the separate unsafe-target test's programmatic helper and explicit navigation semantics intact.
5. If challenge/recovery helpers change, add deterministic controlled-clock/event-order browser tests in tests/clerk-sign-in-navigation.spec.ts at that helper boundary: a challenge arriving after the old observation window but within budget eventually activates; no-challenge immediate success works; disappearing controls after code acceptance do not trigger another submission; a challenge that never completes or a persistent terminal error fails within the single deadline without duplicate submissions. These tests may simulate the helper's observations but must not replace the separate real-provider form journey. Check this file is actually selected by browser-tests.
6. Deliver bounded, allow-listed failure diagnostics (stage, elapsed milliseconds, pathname without query/fragment, booleans for Clerk loaded/session present/challenge visible, bounded known error codes and HTTP status only). Limit collection to 2 seconds and serialized output to 2 KiB; diagnostic collection failure must not mask the original assertion. Never log credentials, verification input, session/user IDs, cookies, storage state, tokens, request/response bodies, arbitrary DOM text, full URLs, raw provider errors or traces containing submitted credentials. If diagnostics code changes, include deterministic assertions that sensitive sentinel inputs and URL queries/fragments never appear and truncation/collection timeout preserves the original failure.
7. Run the complete bound test-heavy workload once the coherent repair is ready. A supported filtered browser-tests run is diagnosis only and cannot establish full-tier PASS. Preserve the empty baseline catalog; classify unrelated failures honestly rather than expanding this repair or inventing exclusions. Record all not-reached/failed steps and applicable target/revision evidence.
